statement: Premium processing (Form I-907, authorized by INA § 286(u)) obligates USCIS to issue an approval notice, denial notice, notice of intent to deny, or request for evidence within the designated timeframe: 15 business days for the designated I-129 nonimmigrant classifications (including E, H-1B, L, O, P, Q, R, and TN) and most designated employment-based immigrant petitions, 45 business days for EB-1C multinational-manager and national-interest-waiver petitions, and 30 business days for the designated change-of-status and employment-authorization applications; an RFE or NOID stops the clock, which restarts in full on receipt of the response, and if USCIS misses the timeframe it refunds the premium fee ($2,965 for most I-129 classifications) while continuing to process the case (8 CFR § 106.4(c), (e), (f)(1), (f)(3)-(4)).
caveat: Premium processing buys adjudicative action, which can be an RFE or a denial rather than an approval; it does not move a consular 221(g) case, USCIS may suspend availability when volumes prevent timely processing, the fee is retained without action if a fraud or misrepresentation investigation opens (8 CFR 106.4(f)(5)), and fees adjust biennially by CPI.
